subject: Culture
title: Death Taboos
description: A quick win: understand Death Taboos.

hook.text: In the US, 70% of people want to die at home. Only 30% do. Nobody wants to talk about it.

buildup.text: Western cultures increasingly avoid death talk. Victorian-era families kept death photos; modern ones hide them.

discovery.text: Sociologist Geoffrey Gorer called this the 'pornography of death'—something everyone knows about but nobody discusses.

twist.text: In Bhutan, people are encouraged to think about death five times a day. Studies show they report higher happiness.

climax.text: 'Death cafes' where strangers discuss mortality over tea have spread to 80 countries since 2011.

punchline.text: Talking about death doesn't increase fear—it reduces it.

quiz.question: Who coined the phrase 'pornography of death'?
